Mit fino.sign entwickeln wir zudem eine eigene E-Signatur-Lösung und erweitern unser Angebot gemeinsam mit unseren Schwesterunternehmen laufend.

Jetzt bauen wir einen neuen Growth-Bereich auf, der Kanzleien aktiv für KanzleiDrive gewinnt – und du gestaltest ihn von Tag eins an mit.

Klingt nach deinem Ding? Dann sollten wir uns kennenlernen!

Deine Aufgaben

Du suchst eine Rolle, in der du nicht verwaltest, sondern aufbaust? Dann bist du bei uns genau richtig. Du verantwortest, wie Kanzleien auf KanzleiDrive aufmerksam und zu Kunden werden – mit Strategie, Kreativität und modernen Tools.

  • Neukundengewinnung: Du entwickelst unsere Go-to-Market- und Vertriebsstrategie und sprichst Steuerkanzleien und Wirtschaftsprüfer aktiv an.

  • Pipeline-Aufbau: Du erzeugst qualifizierte Opportunities für unser Team, misst, was funktioniert, und skalierst die erfolgreichen Kanäle.

  • Marketing & Kampagnen: Du entwickelst Konzepte und Kampagnen, die Kanzleiinhaber und ihre Teams wirklich erreichen – von Content über Webinare bis zu Messen und unserem Partnerprogramm.

  • KI & Automatisierung: Du baust KI-gestützte Prozesse für Lead-Recherche, Datenanreicherung, personalisierte Ansprache und Reporting auf und wählst die passenden Tools aus.

  • Produkt & Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest dich tief in KanzleiDrive ein, um den Nutzen für neue Kanzleien überzeugend zu vermitteln. Erkenntnisse aus Kampagnen und Neukundengesprächen bringst du ins Team – in enger Abstimmung mit unserem Customer Relationship Management und der Produktentwicklung.

  • Content & Sichtbarkeit: Du gestaltest Inhalte für LinkedIn, Instagram und YouTube. Wenn du dich vor der Kamera wohlfühlst, freuen wir uns, wenn du KanzleiDrive dort auch ein Gesicht gibst.

Das bringst du mit

  • Mehrere Jahre Erfahrung in Growth, Business Development, Marketing oder Vertrieb – idealerweise im B2B-SaaS-Umfeld.

  • Nachweisbare Erfolge darin, Leads und Pipeline aufzubauen, nicht nur zu verwalten.

  • Strategischer Blick und Hands-on-Mentalität: Du entwirfst den Plan und setzt die erste Kampagne selbst um.

  • Affinität zu KI-Tools und Freude daran, Abläufe smarter zu machen.

  • Analytische Denkweise: Du arbeitest gern mit Zahlen und leitest daraus Entscheidungen ab.

  • Überzeugende Kommunikation und Freude am Austausch mit Kanzleiinhabern.

  • Selbstständige, strukturierte und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise.

  • Fließende Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Das bieten wir dir

Bei uns bekommst du nicht nur einen neuen Bereich zum Gestalten, sondern auch gute Rahmenbedingungen:

  • Attraktive Vergütung: Solides Grundgehalt plus leistungsabhängige Provision – dein Erfolg zahlt sich direkt aus.

  • Echter Gestaltungsspielraum: Du baust einen Bereich von Grund auf mit – deine Ideen landen nicht in der Schublade, sondern im Markt.

  • Flache Hierarchien & kurze Wege: Direkter Draht und schnelle Entscheidungen.

  • Remote & Homeoffice: Arbeite von zu Hause oder von dort, wo du am besten arbeitest.

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten: Gestalte deinen Tag so, wie er zu deinem Leben passt.

  • Neueste Hardware: Aktuelles MacBook mit top Zubehör.

  • Gesundheit: EGYM Wellpass für Sport und Wellness plus betriebliche Krankenversicherung.

  • Absicherung: Betriebliche Altersvorsorge und vermögenswirksame Leistungen.

  • Extra freie Tage: Heiligabend und Silvester frei, dazu Sonderurlaub zum Geburtstag und zur Hochzeit.

So läuft dein Bewerbungsprozess

Wir halten den Prozess bewusst schlank – und er ist keine Einbahnstraße: Du lernst uns kennen, wir lernen dich kennen.

  1. Bewerbung: Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf, ein Anschreiben ist optional. Gern kannst du Links zu Kampagnen, Content oder Projekten mitschicken, auf die du stolz bist. In der Regel hörst du innerhalb von drei Tagen von uns.

  2. Kennenlernen: In einem lockeren Teams-Call sprechen wir darüber, was dich antreibt und was du bisher bewegt hast. Du bekommst einen ersten Einblick in KanzleiDrive und deinen künftigen Bereich.

  3. Praxis-Case: Du skizzierst, wie du Kanzleien für KanzleiDrive gewinnen würdest, und stellst uns deine Ideen vor. Keine Wochenaufgabe – uns interessiert dein Denkansatz.

  4. Team & Entscheidung: Du lernst das Team und unseren CEO kennen. Danach entscheiden wir schnell und geben dir zeitnah Bescheid.

Klingt spannend? Dann bewirb dich jetzt – wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

Du passt nicht in jedes Raster? Du erfüllst nicht alle Punkte oder kannst nicht viel im Lebenslauf vorweisen? Wenn du überzeugt bist, dass du genau die richtige Person bist, um KanzleiDrive groß zu machen, dann melde dich trotzdem. Für uns zählen Können und Motivation mehr als die Vergangenheit.

Tangany mit Sitz in München ist ein innovatives Technologieunternehmen mit einer marktführenden B2B-Lösung für die Verwahrung digitaler Vermögenswerte (z. B. Kryptowährungen, Stablecoins und anderen tokenisierten Vermögenswerten) in Blockchain-Netzwerken. Unsere Lösung wird bereits von mehr als 50 institutionellen Kunden eingesetzt. Deine Rolle

Du verantwortest das Controlling und die Finanzsteuerung und berichtest an das Management Board.

Das Team ist klein. Deine Expertise und dein Beitrag wirken sich unmittelbar aus: Du arbeitest mit unserer Accountant und unserer Steuerkanzlei z.B. an Themen wie Finanzbuchhaltung, Lohn und Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung; die formale Verantwortung für das Rechnungswesen liegt bei der Geschäftsleitung, Zahlungen geben wir im Vier-Augen-Prinzip frei. In diesem Rahmen bist du die Person, die weiß, wo die Zahlen stehen, warum sie dort stehen und wie sich Ergebnis, Kosten, Liquidität und Eigenmittel entwickeln werden.

Der Kern der Rolle hat zwei Seiten: die regulatorische Pflicht und eine Steuerung, mit der wir jede Finanzfrage jederzeit in wenigen Minuten beantworten können. Business Cases und Investor Reporting kommen dazu und wachsen mit dir.

Heute arbeiten wir vor allem mit DATEV Unternehmen Online und Tableau. Die Steuerung darauf baust du zu großen Teilen neu auf, gern AI-gestützt: Unser AI-Dev-Team setzt mit dir Live-Reporting, Abstimmungen und ein Finanz-Cockpit um.

Aufgaben

  • Den Jahresabschluss nach HGB und RechKredV erstellen, ergänzt um die RechZahlV-Posten für unser Zahlungsgeschäft, und die Prüfung gemeinsam mit unserer Steuerkanzlei und Abschlussprüfer durchführen.

  • Das aufsichtsrechtliche Meldewesen führen und Finanzinformationen nach gesetzlichen Vorgaben unter Begleitung des Compliance-Teams bereitstellen.

  • Regulatorische Planzahlen, etwa die Eigenmittelanforderung, aus der Bilanzplanung ableiten und in Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsleitung laufend überwachen.

  • Cashflow- und Runway-Planung führen und Finanzierungsbedarf früh sichtbar machen.

  • Liquiditäts- und Kontrahentenrisiken in das unternehmensweite Risikocontrolling einbringen und laufend überwachen.

  • Business Cases und Rentabilitätsrechnungen erstellen und Investor-Updates vorbereiten.

  • Eine Kostenstellenstruktur aufbauen, Budgets je Kostenstelle mit den Verantwortlichen festlegen, Kosten, Budgets und KPIs laufend überwachen sowie Live-Reporting und Ad-hoc-Auswertungen für Geschäftsleitung und Budgetverantwortliche bereitstellen und Plan-Ist-Abweichungen analysieren.

  • Aus der Praxiserfahrung heraus Input liefern, um Finanzprozesse, Tools und das interne Kontrollsystem gemeinsam mit unserem AI-Dev-Team auszubauen.

Wen wir suchen

  • Du bist Controller:in (idealerweise aus einem regulierten Institut) und hast Jahresabschluss und Meldewesen selbst verantwortet.

  • Abweichungen erkennst du früh: Wenn sich Eigenmittel, Liquidität oder Kosten in die falsche Richtung bewegen, liegt deine Analyse mit Optionen auf dem Tisch, solange noch Zeit zum Handeln ist.

  • Deine Forecasts halten auch Monate später, und wo sie abweichen, kannst du erklären, warum.

  • Meldefristen und Prüfungsanforderungen baust du so in die Abläufe ein, dass vor dem Stichtag keine Ad-hoc Aktion nötig ist.

  • Prüfer und Risikocontrolling nehmen deine Zahlen als Ausgangspunkt.

  • Stellt die Geschäftsleitung eine Finanzfrage, kannst du schnell und problemlos Antworten geben, weil deine Daten und Auswertungen genau dafür gebaut sind.

  • Du entscheidest auch mit unvollständigen Informationen, sagst klar, wenn etwas nicht geht, und stellst einen Prozess um, sobald er nicht mehr passt.

Qualifikation

Must-Haves

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium oder Ausbildung in Finanzen, Controlling oder einem verwandten Feld.

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung im Controlling oder Rechnungswesen, idealerweise in einem regulierten Institut (nach KWG, ZAG oder MiCAR) oder in der Prüfung entsprechender Institute.

  • Eigenständig erstellte Jahresabschlüsse nach HGB, sowie Erfahrung mit Liquiditäts- und Kontrahentenrisiken sowie Risikotragfähigkeit.

  • Aufbau von Kostenstellenrechnung und Management-Reporting, sicherer Umgang mit DATEV, Excel und Google Sheets inklusive Finanzmodellen und deren Visualisierung, idealerweise mit einem BI-Tool wie Tableau.

  • Offenheit: Reporting mit AI-Werkzeugen neu aufsetzen.

  • Fließend Deutsch und Englisch (C1 oder höher).

Nice-to-Haves

  • Erfahrung mit MiCAR, etwa der Eigenmittelberechnung.

  • FP&A, Business Cases oder Investor-Reporting in einem wachsenden Unternehmen.

  • Erfahrung im aufsichtsrechtlichen Meldewesen nach KWG oder ZAG.

  • Interesse an Krypto und Tokenisierung.

Benefits

Flexibilität & Work-Life-Balance:

  • 30 Tage Urlaub, dazu jeweils ein halber Tag frei an Heiligabend und Silvester, und bei Bedarf zusätzlicher unbezahlter Urlaub, um die Akkus wieder aufzuladen.

  • Zusätzlicher bezahlter Urlaub für frischgebackene Eltern.

Entlohnung und Zusatzleistungen

The Mission: Why We Exist

Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer, healthier lives, using the power of genomics.

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

Role Purpose

Genomic data is some of the most sensitive data there is, and our customers trust us with it. As Senior Application Security Engineer on Mystra, you'll own application security end-to-end across multi-tenant, trillion-row-scale, AI-enabled data platforms.

You'll lead threat modelling and design review with product teams, build the tooling and patterns that make secure codet, and find and fix the vulnerabilities that slip through. You'll do it with security-focused AI tooling, steered by your own expert judgement and intuition, to keep Genomics secure against state-of-the-art threats.

A Day in the Life

  • Leading threat modelling and design reviews for new products and infrastructure, and defining the security invariants every team builds against: tenant isolation, authentication and authorisation, secrets, least privilege, and trust boundaries

  • Building the libraries, patterns, and CI/CD guardrails that make the secure way the easy way, and deciding what is enforced versus advised

  • Building and tuning AI tooling for code analysis, triage, and remediation, and deciding where its output can be trusted and where it must be verified

  • Hunting for vulnerabilities through code review, testing, and proof-of-concept exploits, then running the disclosure programme and driving every finding through to a verified fix

  • Securing our agentic and AI surfaces, from prompt injection and tool boundaries to delegated credentials and tenant-scoped access, and proving the controls hold under adversarial testing

  • Working as an embedded, trusted partner to product teams, SRE, detection and response, the data platform team, and the MystraAI / ML team, unblocking rather than gating

Who You Are

rawCandidates.title: Head of Supply Chain
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
The Role

We are looking for a hands-on Head of Supply Chain to take ownership of how Lumai sources, manages and receives the components that go into our systems. As we move from prototypes to multi-node system deployments and towards our next-generation product, the volume and complexity of what we buy is growing quickly. You will take this work on from our engineering team, allowing them to focus on design and development. In the near term, you will be responsible for sourcing and delivering the components for a major system deployment, working closely with engineering to keep it on schedule and within budget. Alongside this, you will build the supplier relationships, parts management and processes that Lumai will need as it moves towards production.

This is an early role in a growing operations function. You will report into operations leadership, and there is a clear opportunity for the role to grow into a more strategic position as Lumai scales.

What You Will Do

Sourcing and delivery

  • Take ownership of the sourcing of the bill of materials for current system builds, working with engineering to confirm requirements and what is still to be sourced

  • Identify long-lead and single-source items, and put mitigation plans in place

  • Obtain quotes, place and expedite purchase orders, and track deliveries against project plans

  • Work within Lumai's procurement and finance processes

  • Track materials spend against project budgets

Supplier development

  • Identify, assess and qualify suppliers across electronics, PCBs, mechanical parts, contract manufacturing and assembly, and optical components

  • Develop sourcing strategy for future products – single versus dual sourcing, and supplier risk

  • Negotiate pricing, NDAs and supply agreements, working with legal

  • Secure capacity and allocation for constrained parts ahead of volume

  • Build cost models that inform product costing and cost reduction

  • Support new product introduction as designs move from prototype to production

Parts, BoM and lifecycle management

  • Establish Lumai's parts and BoM management process – part numbering, approved manufacturer and supplier lists, and revision and change control – with engineering

  • Introduce a preferred parts list and influence component selection early in design to reduce supply and obsolescence risk

  • Monitor product change and end-of-life notices, and manage the response – last-time buys, qualifying alternates, and flagging redesign needs

  • Maintain a view of supply risk across the BoM

Logistics, stores and quality

  • Manage inbound and outbound logistics, import and customs, and support export control requirements on outbound shipments

  • Set up goods-in, incoming inspection, stores and inventory control appropriate to Lumai's stage

  • Select and run lightweight tools for parts, BoM and inventory management that will scale with the company

  • Define supplier quality expectations, track supplier performance, and manage non-conformances and returns

What We Are Looking For

Must-have

  • At least three years' experience in supply chain, procurement or operations within a hardware company – such as electronics, semiconductors or data centre systems

  • Hands-on experience sourcing components, from quotation through to delivery

  • Practical experience of BoM management, part lifecycle and component obsolescence

  • Experience setting up or improving supply chain processes and tools

  • Confident negotiating with suppliers and building long-term supplier relationships

  • Comfortable doing transactional work day to day while building strategy and process for the longer term

  • Able to work closely with engineers and understand technical specifications

Desirable

  • Experience taking hardware from prototype to production, including working with contract manufacturers

  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment

  • Knowledge of optical, photonic or optoelectronic components

  • Familiarity with import, customs and export control processes

  • Experience with ERP, PLM or inventory management systems

About Lumai

Lumai is the optical compute company building the next generation of AI infrastructure. Spun out of optics research at the University of Oxford in 2021, we compute with light instead of electrons. Our 3D optical technology carries out the matrix multiplications at the heart of AI inside beams of light travelling through free space, which lets it go beyond the limits of both silicon GPUs and integrated photonics.

In April 2026 we launched the world's first optical computing system to run billion-parameter large language models in real time. Our first optical computing server is now available for evaluation by hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprises and research institutions.

Our work won the Falling Walls Award for Science Breakthrough of the Year 2025 and 'Best Overall Technology' at the OCP Future Technologies Symposium. We are headquartered in Oxford.

Why Lumai

You'll work on a new kind of computer. Optical computing for AI has been promised for decades. We have a working system running real models, and the hard part left is taking it to volume.

Your work ships. We are moving from first product to volume production, so what you build this year goes into the servers our customers run.

You'll work across disciplines. Optical engineers, machine learning researchers, and hardware and software engineers solve problems together. You will learn things that don't appear on your job description.

The work matters beyond Lumai. AI's appetite for energy is one of the defining constraints of the next decade. Our mission is sustainable intelligence at global scale: AI that is faster, cheaper to run and far less power-hungry.

You'll join early. You'll have a real say in how we build the product, the team and the way we work.

Equal Opportunity

Lumai is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions based on skills, experience and potential, and we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. If you need an adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, let us know and we will do our best to support you.

Hozah makes parking automatic. Cameras recognise a car as it arrives and payment happens by itself when it leaves: no tickets, no barriers, no apps. Drivers get parking that's fair and effortless; landowners get better-run car parks, happier visitors and more revenue.

We're an award-winning, fast-growing UK tech company, named PayTech Company of the Year and, two years running, Cleantech of the Year in the Deloitte UK Technology Fast 50. Today we run car parks for shopping centres, councils, the NHS, hotels and more, and we're scaling fast, with high standards, low ego and never at the expense of fairness.

The Role

We're looking for an exceptional Head of Marketing & Demand Generation to lead the next stage of Hozah's growth. You'll build the engine that generates our leads and new business, own our brand and everything people see, hear and experience of Hozah, and lead the team that makes it happen.

This is a senior, high-impact role for an AI-first marketer and proven lead and demand generator who is as strong on brand as on the numbers. You'll shape our marketing strategy with our Chief Growth Officer, keep our sales pipeline full of qualified leads and build a brand that's known, trusted and chosen. As Hozah scales, your team, your remit and your influence grow with it.

You'll report to our Co-Founder/Chief Growth Officer, and lead and grow our in-house marketing team. The role is based in Croydon, next to East Croydon Station, working hybrid with at least three office days a week. Target start: early 2027.

What You'll Own

  • Demand generation. The engine that generates qualified leads, pipeline and new business for our sales team, across digital, content, outreach and events.

  • Brand. Our brand, positioning and voice, and how Hozah looks, sounds and feels everywhere: online, in print, at events and in the car parks we run.

  • Reputation and awareness. Making Hozah the name the industry knows and trusts, through PR, content, social media, thought leadership and events.

  • Sales materials. Everything our sales team uses to win, from proposals and presentations to case studies.

  • Clients. Marketing that keeps our clients close.

  • A high-performing team. Leading, developing and growing our in-house team, and setting the standard for everything marketing produces.

  • Results. The marketing budget and the targets that matter: leads, pipeline and new business, alongside brand awareness and reputation.

Who We're Looking For

  • A track record of building, leading and developing high-performing B2B marketing teams.

  • A proven lead and demand generator: you've built B2B programmes that delivered qualified leads, pipeline and new business, and can show the numbers.

  • An AI-first way of working: you use AI across your marketing every day and have built AI workflows a team relies on.

  • Experience owning a brand end to end and growing its awareness and reputation.

  • Strong commercial judgement: you put budget where it makes the biggest difference and can show the return.

  • Exceptional craft: a sharp writer and editor with a strong eye for brand and design.

  • Strong technical knowledge of marketing tools, including HubSpot and Google Analytics.

  • The presence to shape strategy with a leadership team, and the drive to turn it into results.

Desirable:

  • Marketing to property owners, asset managers, managing agents or multi-site organisations.

  • PR and thought leadership in a specialist industry.

  • Events, sponsorships and experiential marketing.

  • Digital marketing across SEO, AI visibility, paid and social.

  • Client or retention marketing.

Parking industry experience is not required.

What You Get In Return

  • Real headroom: a senior role that grows as Hozah does.

  • An award-winning product and a story worth telling.

  • Free breakfast and lunch every day, quarterly socials, a personal development plan, and 24/7 support for you and your family through our employee assistance programme.

  • Hybrid working: at least three days a week in our Croydon office, next to East Croydon Station, and the rest from home.

Hiring Process

  1. 45–60 minute introductory Teams call with our Head of Talent Acquisition.

  2. 75 minute structured Teams interview with our Chief Growth Officer.

  3. An approximately two-hour practical assessment at our Croydon office covering a marketing plan, team priorities, a brand review, interpreting results and using AI live, with fictional information.

  4. References before an offer.

We're hiring a Revenue Operations Executive to keep HubSpot and our market and client data accurate, complete and useful. You'll research companies and contacts, run data enrichment, clean and import data, make sure leads reach the right person, support marketing with lists and tracking, and produce agreed reports.

It's a hands-on development role for someone with strong practical HubSpot skills and real care for data, with clear processes, coaching and room to take on more as you grow.

You'll report to our Head of Revenue Operations, who is also joining. The role is based in Croydon, next to East Croydon Station, working hybrid with at least three office days a week. Target start: January 2027.

What You'll Do

  • Market and contact data. Research companies and contacts, run agreed enrichment and data refreshes, and note where every record came from.

  • HubSpot records and leads. Clean and import data, merge duplicates, fix bad entries, apply the right owner, stage and tags, and route new leads to the right person.

  • Reporting. Produce agreed reports on schedule and flag anything that doesn't add up.

Who We're Looking For

  • Careful handling of data: spotting duplicates and inconsistencies, checking accuracy and investigating gaps.

  • Confidence with technology, large lists, imports and routine reports.

  • Clear communication, reliable follow-through and the judgement to ask for help when needed.

  • An appetite to learn new tools, including AI, and improve how work gets done.

Useful but not essential:

  • Experience in revenue, sales or marketing operations, CRM or sales administration.

  • Experience with prospecting and enrichment tools.

  • Experience with HubSpot forms, lists or marketing emails, or HubSpot Academy certifications.

  • Simple automation, such as HubSpot workflows.

We welcome experienced sales, marketing or commercial administrators moving into revenue operations. Parking industry experience is not required.

What You Get In Return

  • Hands-on experience across market data, HubSpot, lead management and reporting.

  • Coaching from our Head of Revenue Operations, clear processes and scope to take on more responsibility.

  • Hybrid working: at least three days a week in our Croydon office, next to East Croydon Station, and the rest from home.

Hiring Process

  1. A 20–30 minute introductory Teams call with our Head of Talent Acquisition.

  2. A 60 minute structured Teams interview with our Chief Growth Officer.

  3. A 90 minute practical assessment at our Croydon office covering HubSpot tasks, contact research, data clean-up and explaining a report, using dummy data. No take-home assignment.

  4. References before an offer.

rawCandidates.title: Head of Security
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
About Us

Basecamp Research is building frontier AI for therapeutic design. We believe the future of medicine lies in reprogramming the body to repair itself, and we design the models and the medicines to teach it how.

Our EDEN models are trained on BaseData and our Trillion Gene Atlas (TGA), the world's largest proprietary genomic dataset, with over 10B genes collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries across all seven continents. This gives our AI models access to genetic diversity that doesn't exist in public databases, and enables EDEN to design cell and gene therapies, enzymes, and peptides directly from information about a disease. Our pipeline of EDEN-designed therapeutics, beginning with in vivo cell therapy, is advancing towards clinical development.

In September 2026 we closed an oversubscribed $140M Series C led by S32, with participation from NVIDIA, Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio, European Tech Collective, Firebrand River Capital, King Philanthropies, NATO Innovation Fund, Redalpine, Rockefeller Foundation, Singular, Sovereign AI and True Ventures. We have offices and labs in London and Boston, we partner with biopharma companies and academic institutions worldwide, and our work has been recognised by Fast Company's Top 10 Most Innovative Companies in Biotech, the FT-backed Sifted AI100 list of Europe's leading AI startups as well as Barclays Eagle Labs Ones to watch, AI100.

At Basecamp Research, we pride ourselves on being a lean collaborative and global team with extremely specialist and unique skills. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today.

The Role

We're seeking a Head of Security to join our team in London and own the security of Basecamp Research: our data, our models, our locations and our people.

We hold one of the most valuable proprietary biological datasets in the world and the models trained on it, and we operate labs, field expeditions and partnerships across more than 30 countries. Our proprietary data and IP is incredibly powerful therefore we have a duty to our investors, employees, governments and partners to do everything in our power to protect it and use it for positive outcomes. Our security function will take the lead on cyber security and AI safety, and we have strong technical controls across our estate, working with governmental and commercial partners. We now need a new leader to build on our security foundations and develop them into a complete, mature security programme.

This is a hands-on role with a wide remit: cyber and infrastructure security with the platform team, AI and agentic security across the company, and personnel, insider risk, physical and travel security with the People and Operations teams

What you'll own

  • Security strategy. Threat model, roadmap, policies, security culture and reporting to leadership.

  • Cyber and infrastructure security. Vulnerability management, network, cloud and on-prem hardening, supply chain risk, incident response.

  • AI security. Agentic systems, isolated research environments, model and data protection and AI safety risks across the company.

  • People and physical security. Insider risk, personnel security, investigations, threat intelligence, office and lab security, and duty of care for staff in the field.

  • Certifications and providers. Certifications like ISO 27001 and ISO 42001, partner due diligence, and external security vendors.

About you

  • Experience building or leading a security programme against sophisticated, well-resourced adversaries, in government, defence, protective security or a targeted company, with a working knowledge of threat actors and their tactics.

  • Hands-on. You will personally run vulnerability management, review infrastructure designs, lead incident and crisis response and write policy.

  • Strong technical depth across identity, endpoint, network, cloud and on-prem infrastructure and application security, working with engineers and researchers to secure lab and research environments without slowing the science.

  • Experience running training and awareness programmes to foster a positive culture of shared responsibility in relation to personnel, insider risk and physical security that protect IP while remaining proportionate and trusted by staff.

  • You take responsibility for the outcome. If a problem requires learning something new or working outside your usual area, you do it.

  • Discretion, judgement and personal integrity. You will handle sensitive matters that require pragmatism coupled with a strong moral compass. Collaborative and low ego. In a small team everyone depends on what you build.

Nice to have

  • Experience with national security or cybersecurity bodies

  • Experience taking a company through ISO 27001, and familiarity with ISO 42001, ISO 31030 and UK government security frameworks.

  • Experience with the security of ML research environments, AI safety and agentic systems.

  • Experience running travel risk programmes for staff in high-risk locations.

  • Experience in life sciences, including lab environments and regulated data.

What we offer in return

Impactful Mission: This is a rare chance to do work that genuinely matters. You'll join a talented, fast-moving team, access unique biological datasets at scale, and see your contributions shape real breakthroughs in AI and curative therapeutics.

Collaborative Culture: You'll be surrounded by world-class engineers, scientists, and researchers who care deeply about their work and about each other. With offices in London and Boston, we've built a flexible, cross-functional environment where personal development and real ownership aren't just talking points.

High Growth: We truly believe in investing in our top talent, we make coaching available to team members during steep growth journeys and we have twice yearly promotion opportunities. People who are really successful here own it and go directly to solve problems at pace and we ensure reward increases with impact.

Comprehensive Benefits: We've built a benefits package people value. That means competitive salary, equity, and private healthcare with no medical history exclusions so strong that most employees' family members opt into our plan over their own. We also offer Carrot Fertility with IVF stipend, salary sacrifice pension, bike to work scheme, life insurance, and more.

Do you want to join our team? Then we'd love to hear from you.

We are committed to equal opportunity employment regardless of ethnic or national origin, race, religion, sex, age, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, gender identity or any other basis. If you have a disability or additional need that needs accommodating do let us know.

When a finance team leads with its craft, they make better decisions and steer the business with more confidence. In order to do that, the busywork that comes with expense management needs to move out the way.

That’s why we built a spend management platform that streamlines the whole process, from employee spending to approvals and reconciliation. Finance teams get clarity and control of all the numbers and data in one place and employees get an experience that they actually enjoy.

The word “Pleo” in Greek means “more than you’d expect,” and that mindset has driven our growth since 2015 and our 40,000+ customers. Today we’re 750+ people from over 65 nationalities who take pride in understanding customer needs, turning complex problems into simple solutions, challenging the way things are done, and aiming for the highest outcome. We haven’t got everything figured out, but we’re committed to developing and delivering an experience as elevated as the craft of finance.

As a Staff Backend Engineer, you'll take technical ownership of complex business domains, designing, building, and evolving scalable, reliable backend services for our enterprise spend management platform.

What you'll be working on:

  • Designing and operating distributed systems, event-driven architectures, and cloud-native services.

  • Applying Domain-Driven Design (DDD) to model complex business domains and define clear service boundaries.

  • Building maintainable systems following Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and similar architectural principles.

  • Designing APIs, service integrations, and reliable asynchronous workflows using technologies such as Temporal.

  • Designing secure authentication and authorization solutions, applying standards such as OAuth 2.0, OIDC, and WebAuthn, as well as fine-grained authorization models.

  • Ensuring scalability, security, observability, and resilience in production.

  • Continuously improving shared libraries, project structure, development tooling, and automated quality assurance practices to promote consistency, reusability, and maintainability across services.

  • Driving architectural decisions, evaluating trade-offs, and mentoring other engineers.

  • Leveraging AI extensively but responsibly, including developing guardrails, agent harnesses, and tooling to maintain engineering quality in a fast-paced environment.



We primarily use Node.js with TypeScript, with Java and Kotlin as a nice to have. Above all, strong engineering fundamentals matter more to us than experience with a particular language. Our technology stack also includes Temporal, SpiceDB, PostgreSQL, Kafka, and Redis.

This is a 80/20 hands-on technical leadership role, combining deep engineering work with architectural ownership and influence across teams.
Remote, but travel to Amsterdam or other offsite meetings in Europe might occasionally be requested

Your colleagues would say you

  • Lead by example and raise the bar with pragmatism and care.

  • Enjoy breaking down complex problems, gathering input, and driving to a solution.

Show me the benefits

  • Access to LinkedIn Learning - acquire new skills, stay abreast of industry trends and fuel your personal and professional development continuously

About Zable

Zable (formerly Lendable) is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.

Zable was founded on the belief that smarter technology is the solution to lower cost, more transparent consumer finance. Our proprietary foundation models analyse thousands of data points in seconds, drawing a more complete picture of individual financial behaviour. This means we can make better risk decisions, widening access and lowering prices.

The Zable credit card harnesses this technology to deliver better borrowing for three million people. Through our superapp, Zable connects this card to a single platform which makes it effortless to manage credit, get a loan, refinance existing borrowing, switch utilities, get a mobile plan and save more.

Zable is now the number one issuer of new credit cards and personal loans in the UK, but we’ve barely got started. Next, we’re taking our approach to some of the biggest markets in the world - the US and Mexico - where hundreds of millions of people are underserved by outdated bank processes.

Zable is a high-growth FinTech building its security operations capability deliberately. As a Senior Security Operations Analyst, you will triage and respond to security alerts, help improve the quality of the detections behind them, and lead the response when a security event becomes an incident.

You will investigate alerts and escalations from our MSSP, tune our monitoring so that it finds more of what matters and less of what doesn’t, and act as a trusted Incident Commander for security incidents, from declaration through to post-incident review. You will work with Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders, and you will be credible with all of them.

AI is used widely across the business, in how we build software, run operations and serve customers, and that changes both what security incidents look like and how quickly we can respond to them. You will use AI and automation as a normal part of your work, and you will be able to investigate and respond to incidents where AI tooling is the cause, the target or the route in.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone with hands-on SOC experience and a track record of commanding incidents.

1. Alert Triage & Monitoring

  • Triage and investigate alerts across our SIEM, EDR, identity and cloud tooling, taking escalations from our MSSP’s first-line team.

  • Reduce false positives and alert fatigue by tuning detection rules, thresholds and suppressions.

  • Utilise AI and automation to speed up triage, enrichment and response, and to remove repetitive manual work from the analyst workflow.

2. Incident Command & Response

  • Command security incidents, coordinating technical response, decision-making and communications across Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders. Give clear, timely updates to executives during live incidents.

  • Lead or support technical investigation and containment across endpoint, identity and cloud (AWS/GCP) environments, including incidents involving AI use, such as prompt injection, or credentials exposed through AI-generated code.

  • Run blameless post-incident reviews, track actions to closure, and feed lessons back into detection, playbooks and controls.

  • Take part in the out-of-hours on-call rota.

3. Operational Reporting & Assurance

  • Track and report SecOps metrics that reflect reality, such as alert quality, time to triage, time to contain, incident volumes and root causes.

  • Maintain accurate incident records and evidence in our incident management platform to support audit and assurance activity.

  • Build working relationships with Engineering, Platform and IT Systems so that incident response is practised before it is needed.

  • Proven incident command: Demonstrable experience leading significant security incidents as Incident Commander or lead responder, from declaration to resolution and review. You can describe incidents you have run, the decisions you made and what you changed afterwards.

  • Technical investigation skills: Solid hands-on SOC/DFIR experience, including log analysis, endpoint and identity investigation, and cloud incident response in AWS or GCP.

  • AI fluency: You understand how AI use creates security risk, including data exposure, agent misuse and AI-assisted attacks, and you can investigate and contain incidents that involve it.

  • AI-first ways of working: You already use AI and automation to speed up your own work, whether in investigation, enrichment, detection engineering or reporting, and you can judge when to trust the output and when to check it.

  • Composure and influence: You stay calm and structured under pressure, and can direct engineers and senior stakeholders without formal authority over them.

  • Communication: You can brief a senior leader in plain language during a live incident, and write a post-incident report that an engineer, an auditor and a board member can each use.

  • Pragmatism: You understand that security supports a business moving quickly, and you balance risk, speed and proportionality in your decisions.

  • Regulated environment awareness (desirable): Experience in financial services or another regulated sector, including incident reporting and evidence expectations.

  • Certifications (desirable, not required): GCIH, GCFA, GCIA, or equivalent practical experience.

APMs at Zable take ownership of their product changes, working closely with teams across Engineering, Credit, Finance and Operations to solve problems and take the business to the next level.

You'll have the opportunity to solve complex problems, scale impactful products, and help shape the future of our lending experience. If you're excited by fintech and enjoy turning data and customer insight into great products, we'd love to hear from you.

  • Improving repayment performance: Running experiments to help more customers pay on time, from choosing repayment dates to how and when we remind people to pay.

  • Testing and learning with customers: Running customer research and testing ideas to understand what people need, how they behave and what works best.

  • Taking products from idea to launch: Working across Engineering, Data Science and Operations to understand the impact of new features, coordinate their rollout and make sure they work for both customers and the business.

  • Increasing impact with AI: Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

Don't worry if you don't meet every single one of the criteria. We'd love to hear from great candidates who are curious, proactive and excited to learn.

  • Experience: 1–2 years in product, or 2-3 years in strategy, analytics, consulting or similar roles, ideally with experience working closely with product or delivery teams to get things done.

  • Data-driven: You're comfortable working with data and can use SQL or Python to investigate problems and answer your own questions.

  • AI-native: You're already experimenting with AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex in your work or side projects, and are excited to see how far they can take you.

  • Hands-on: You're happy to roll up your sleeves and pick up the small jobs. In a lean product team, no task is beneath your attention.

  • Adaptable: You enjoy variety and like that no two days look quite the same.

  • Bonus: Experience in lending, payments, fintech or a fast-growing startup.

AI at Zable

We want to build the most AI-forward financial services company in the world. PMs here make their own dashboards to answer questions that used to need an analyst, build their own agents and workflows to take care of repetitive work, and ship straightforward changes to production themselves.   • Using AI and digital tools to resolve queries faster and more accurately

  • Comfort with digital tools and picking up new technology, including AI-driven platforms

  • Build a growing evidence base on price elasticity from these tests to inform future pricing decisions

  • Validate that implemented pricing and strategy changes are working as intended once deployed in production, flagging and investigating any unexpected behaviour.

Evaluate expansion opportunities:

  • Support the evaluation of new product, channel and segment opportunities by extracting and analysing data and contributing to commercial models

  • Help maintain assessment frameworks and tooling so that evaluations are consistent and repeatable

Partnerships and sponsorships will be central to how we grow, and we’re building the team to make that happen. As our Growth Partnerships Manager, you’ll shape the strategy and the budget, not just manage the day-to-day. Reporting to the Head of Growth Partnerships, you’ll define our commercial approach, decide where partnership spend goes, and take every deal from first conversation to live activation: agreeing terms, making sure campaigns land well, and keeping partners engaged. You’ll also make the case for each investment, with the data to back it, to senior leadership.

This is a senior seat for someone who enjoys both the creative and the analytical sides of partnerships. You’ll have real budget responsibility, model payback economics, and bring colleagues with you on the big calls. If you think about CPA, rev share and LTV:CAC as naturally as you think about relationships, you’ll feel at home here.

What we're looking for:

Essential:

  • 5+ years in partnerships, affiliate marketing, sponsorships, BD or growth roles for a consumer brand, including time spent shaping commercial strategy, not just executing it

  • Fluent in core acquisition performance metrics, CPA, Revenue share, LTV, ROI and blended CAC, and comfortable moving between them when structuring a deal

  • Working knowledge of channel economics: payback period, cohort behaviour, and how partnership spend compares against other acquisition channels

  • Direct experience running affiliate and/or influencer partnership end to end, including commercial negotiation (not just relationship management)

  • Track record of running activations end-to-end and delivering measurable results

  • Strong account / relationship management skills

  • Comfortable with the data, channel economics, attribution and ROI

  • Highly organised and detail-oriented, you can run multiple activations in parallel

  • Strong commercial communicator, you can hold your own with senior partners and senior internal stakeholders alike

  • Experience setting and owning a partnerships budget or channel P&L, with the judgement to reprioritise spend as performance data comes in

  • Comfortable presenting strategy and performance to senior leadership, and defending investment decisions with data

  • Demonstrable use of AI in your workflow

Desirable:

  • Experience in fintech or financial services

  • Experience with sport, entertainment, media or large brand sponsorships

  • Experience with an affiliate network or tracking platform (e.g. Impact, Awin, CJ, Partnerize) and reading platform-level reporting unassisted

  • Experience with affiliate, influencer or embedded finance partnerships

  • Some deal structuring experience

  • Experience line-managing or mentoring a more junior partnerships or affiliate executive

  • A natural relationship-builder, partners trust you, and so does your team

  • A strategic thinker as much as a doer, you can zoom out to set the plan, then zoom back in to execute it yourself

  • Commercially literate first, relationship-led second, you measure success in growth, not vanity

  • A strong project manager, you keep things moving and on-budget

  • Data-fluent , you build your own view on what’s working from raw performance data, not just a dashboard summary

  • Hands-on and resourceful, you make things happen

Every email and notification we send is part of how customers experience Zable, and a 5.0★ Trustpilot rating across more than 100,000 reviews sets a high bar for it: communication has to be clear, timely and honest. As our Senior Product Manager for CRM & Growth, you'll own the products and systems that shape how customers hear from us across their lifecycle, from first interaction through to retention and reactivation.

Product here isn't backlog grooming. The trade-offs are commercial as much as they are user-facing: engagement, retention, conversion, cost to serve and customer experience all pull against each other, and you'll make the calls. There will always be more good ideas than capacity, so sharp prioritisation is central to the job. The role also has a real technical edge. Messaging reliability, deliverability and platform integrations are part of what you'll own, so you'll need to be comfortable going deep with engineers. Teams here are small relative to the size of the book we run, so you'll carry more scope and ownership than the same title would at a larger, more layered company.

  • Owning the roadmap and outcomes for our CRM and lifecycle product: onboarding, engagement, retention and reactivation

  • Prioritising a pipeline of competing opportunities across CRM, growth, deliverability and platform work, weighing expected impact, effort and risk, and being clear about what we won't do

  • Taking products and channel improvements from problem definition through to launch and iteration, owning both the product and technical decisions alongside Engineering

  • Defining the metrics that matter and making the commercial trade-offs between growth, retention, cost and customer experience, and making sure performance is measurable end to end, from tracking and data flows through to dashboards the wider business can trust

  • Running an experimentation programme: writing clear hypotheses, designing A/B tests, and using SQL and our data to measure true incremental impact

  • Treating email deliverability and messaging reliability as product concerns, working with Engineering on infrastructure, platform integrations and cost efficiency

  • Shaping requirements with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Risk and Compliance so that what we ship is effective and meets the standards expected of a regulated lender

  • Holding a high bar for what customers receive: clear, honest content, well-tested design, and rigorous checks before and after launch.

  • 5+ years in product management, with substantial experience in CRM, lifecycle, messaging or growth for a consumer product at meaningful scale

  • Excellent prioritisation: a clear, defensible way of ranking competing opportunities by expected impact, effort and risk, the confidence to say no, and the ability to explain trade-offs to stakeholders

  • A track record of owning measurable outcomes in engagement, retention or revenue, not just shipping features

  • Strong SQL and analytical skills, and experience designing and interpreting A/B tests, with the habit of measuring impact rigorously rather than relying on vanity metrics

  • Enough technical depth to work credibly with engineers on messaging infrastructure, deliverability and platform integrations, and clear communication across technical and commercial audiences

  • Experience in financial services or another regulated industry

  • Experience launching a new channel or capability end to end, such as push notifications across mobile and web

We’re entering a once-in-a-company moment: a major step-change in our D2C marketing investment, a full rebrand of the company and product under the Zable brand, and a marketing function being built out at pace. This is one of the most exciting marketing builds in UK fintech right now, with the financial strength, customer base, and product depth to back it up.

Direct Marketing is one of our highest-potential channels and we’re hiring a leader to turn it into a scaled, precise, and defensible growth engine. We’re looking for a Head of Direct Marketing to own the channel end-to-end: creative, sends, logistics, offers, and reporting, sourcing the data pipeline and user-data enrichment that let us target the right customer, with the right offer, at the right moment. Addressed direct mail is the core today, and you’ll have the scope to extend into other formats.

You'll lead the channel's dedicated analysts and work with our creative team. Your job is to set the direction: decide who we mail, with what offer and when, commission and challenge the selection and response models, and hold every campaign to CAC and LTV targets.

Standalone direct marketing roles with this kind of budget and autonomy are rare. If you've got significant experience in acquisition mail and want to build and extend a channel your own way, at a profitable business with the product range and analytical capabilities to make it work, this is the role.

What we’re looking for:

Essential:

  • 5+ years in direct marketing, including at least 2–3 years owning an acquisition DM programme end to end: strategy, budget, data, production and results.

  • A track record of mailing cold prospects at meaningful scale. You'll be able to talk through the volumes, budgets, response rates and CPAs you've been accountable for.

  • Commercial ownership: you build the business case, forecast volumes and returns, and judge results on a marginal CAC basis rather than vanity metrics.

  • Experience procuring data: working with data suppliers on list selection, screening, enrichment and cost.

  • Deep knowledge of the DM supply chain: print, lettershop, Royal Mail products (Advertising Mail, Mailmark, partially addressed, door drops) and suppression (MPS, goneaways, deceased).

  • A strongly commercial approach. You build the business case, forecast volumes and returns, own the channel P&L, and measure spend on CAC, ROI and payback rather than pieces mailed.

  • Strong analytical judgement. You design test cells and holdouts, read results critically, and understand response and propensity modelling well enough to brief analysts, challenge their work and turn it into mailing decisions.

  • Experience managing suppliers: tendering, negotiating, setting SLAs and keeping several partners to schedule.

  • The ability to run a multi-drop campaign calendar across products, segments, creative, compliance sign-off, production and mail dates.

  • Experience leading analysts and working closely with creative teams.

  • A clear communicator who earns the trust of finance, risk, compliance and data teams.

  • Demonstrable use of AI in your workflow.

Desirable:

  • Experience in acquisition mail in financial services, especially credit cards or loans, including prescreened or pre-approved offers and risk-based targeting.

  • Experience standing up a data pipeline or enrichment stack (first-party + third-party / bureau data)

  • Experience building a channel or function from scratch

  • Background hiring and developing an analytics or design team

You’re a good fit if you’re:

  • Acquisition-minded: you're energised by finding new customers, not re-contacting existing ones.

  • Commercially driven: you measure success in incremental LTV and payback, not response rate alone.

  • A first-principles thinker: you argue from data and clean experiments, not received wisdom

  • Organised: you can run several drops across multiple suppliers and still hit mailing deadlines.

  • Energised by greenfield: you’d rather build the engine than tune someone else’s

What you’ll be doing

Strategy and commercials

  • Own the direct marketing strategy and set volume, response and payback targets anchored to LTV.

  • Own the channel P&L: forecasting, budget and CAC/LTV discipline.

  • Decide how far and how fast to scale, based on the economics.

Data and targeting

  • Source and buy prospect data from bureaus and brokers, and combine it with our first-party data.

  • Direct the analysts building the response and propensity models that decide who we mail, with what offer and when.

  • Work with risk analysts to shape offers around eligibility and lifetime value.

Campaigns and supplier management

  • Plan and run the campaign calendar, from data selection to the mail landing on doormats.

  • Select, negotiate with and manage print and postal suppliers on cost, quality and turnaround.

  • Brief the creative team on packs, copy and offers, and take them through compliance sign-off.

Reporting & Team

  • Build the reporting that ties sends to funnel, revenue and LTV and report on channel performance

  • Partner with data, product, risk, finance and the creative team to unlock targeting and offers

  • Hire and develop the team as the channel scales, and use AI to let a small team punch above its weight

About the role

This role is for someone wanting to start a career in operations within a financial services firm. You'll join as a Graduate focused on working complaints and train to become a fully competent Complaints Officer, investigating and resolving our more complex customer interactions across loans, cards and auto-finance. A critical role to help the business understand how it can serve customers better.

This is a casework role. From early on you will hold your own caseload, speak to customers directly, make decisions on whether we got it right, and put things right where we didn't. You will be supported through structured training, coaching and quality feedback as you develop in the role

Some of the areas you'll delve into are:

  • The regulatory framework for complaints: FCA regulation, the DISP rules, Consumer Duty, and how the guidance is applied to real cases.

  • Investigation technique: gathering evidence, interrogating system records and call recordings, and testing what actually happened against what should have happened.

  • Decision making and redress: reaching fair and objective outcomes, and calculating and explaining any compensation due.

  • Customer communication: writing final response letters that break complex issues down into plain English.

  • The Financial Ombudsman Service: how cases are referred, how FOS reaches its view, and how we apply those learnings to future cases.

  • Root cause and feedback: spotting the product and process failures behind complaints and feeding them back to frontline and product teams.

Reporting to a Complaints Manager within the Operations Team, you will be responsible for a live caseload and for the quality of the decisions you make on it.

No prior complaints experience needed, we care about how you think, not what you already know. This role requires an ability to learn quickly, work to deadlines and support our customers effectively.

Your team's objectives

Zable aims to resolve all complaints promptly, ensuring that they are investigated diligently and fairly for customers. We are committed to providing excellent customer service and to reaching the right outcomes for our customers.

Feedback is an important part of how we evolve as a business. The team is encouraged to speak up, take each complaint on its own merits and provide valuable insight back into the business so we can improve and grow.

Our ability to handle complaints effectively for our customers and therefore for us as a business has never been more important than now, as we expand our existing products in the UK and US financial markets.

What you'll be doing

  • Investigating and resolving complaints about our loans, cards and auto-finance products, taking each case on its own merits

  • Self-managing a varied and increasingly complex caseload: prioritising cases, choosing the best contact mechanism for each customer, and working efficiently enough to meet our KPI minimum standards

  • Communicating with complainants in writing and by phone — managing expectations, handling difficult situations with tact and professionalism, and finding solutions to the issues raised

  • Writing professional final response letters that set out our decision, our rationale and the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • Following our complaint handling standards and keeping clear records, making sure every decision is backed by demonstrable evidence and a documented rationale

  • Working to resolve complaints without the customer needing to refer to FOS, and applying the learnings from both internal and FOS outcomes to future cases

  • Feeding back to frontline and product teams on the product and process improvements your cases surface, across Operations and the wider business

  • Strong organisation and self-management - you can hold a caseload, prioritise it and work to deadlines without being chased

A lot of the work of getting customers through the door is in place. The next stage is about what happens once they’re in: helping them pay on time, giving more credit to the ones who earn it, getting people back on track when they fall behind, and ensuring an intuitive user experience across channels.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

About the role

We're hiring a Associate Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. One week you might be sizing an opportunity, the next week sitting with the ops team to understand why customers are calling, or putting a rough version of an idea in front of real customers before anyone builds the proper one. We care more about how quickly we learn than how polished the first attempt looks.

What you'll work on

  • Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

  • Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

  • Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

  • Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

rawCandidates.descriptionText:
Who We Are

Zefir is building an AI autopilot for home sales in Europe, starting in France. Our agent runs each sale from listing to closing. It coordinates buyers, sellers, and local brokers, manages listings across property portals, and handles the paperwork. We help homeowners sell for the best price on a timeline that works for them.

We’ve raised €60 million from Sequoia Capital and other leading investors. Our goal is to help millions of Europeans take the next step in their lives, whether that means moving to a new city for work or making room for a growing family.

The mission

Zefir sells homes with an AI agent, but our growth is still run mostly by hand.

Every week, someone reads the dashboards, works out why bookings dropped on Tuesday, moves budget from one channel to another, asks for new creatives and fixes a broken tracking tag. Each of these tasks follows rules we could write down. Your job is to write them down and hand them to agents: software that watches the funnel all day, explains what changed and makes the routine fixes itself, within limits the team sets.

You'll learn those rules by doing the work first. From day one you run our acquisition: around €1M of spend a month on Meta, Google and new channels, in a business growing about 2.5x a year. The number you answer for is the expected margin of each call we book. Cheap leads that never become sellers don't count. Anything you still do by hand after six months is a task you haven't automated yet.

Few places let you try this. Most companies spending this much are too slow to hand decisions to agents, and most companies that would let you are too small to give the agents anything to decide. Here you get both, and nobody has written the playbook yet.

 

What you'll build

Horizon 1: Master the engine (first 90 days)

  • Own the numbers: run the weekly read of the acquisition funnel (spend, leads, qualified sellers, booked calls, expected margin per call) vs plan. Explain every gap down to its root cause and drive the actions that close it.

  • Make the data trustworthy: build the single source of truth with our Data team, set the counting and attribution rules, and own the conversion signals we send to Meta, Google and every new platform, including how we count and value bookings made by our AI sales agent as it takes over the qualification call.

  • Find the first levers: landing pages, keyword quality, creative performance, base activation, new channels. Ship fast, measure honestly.

Horizon 2: Automate the loop (months 3 to 9)

  • Agents that see: automated monitoring, anomaly detection and daily variance diagnosis, so problems are caught in hours, not weeks.

  • Agents that decide: explicit, testable rules and models for budget allocation, creative cut and scale, bidding signals and activation timing.

  • Agents that act: campaign changes, CRM activations and experiments executed automatically within guardrails, with humans approving what matters.

Horizon 3: Scale the autopilot (9 months and beyond)

  • Close the loop between creative, media, CRM and our AI sales agent, so every learning flows back into every channel.

  • Run experimentation on autopilot: hypotheses generated, tests launched, results read and rolled out continuously.

  • Define the operating model of a growth team where agents do the execution and people do the thinking, and grow the team that runs it.

 

Why this role

  • Impact you can measure in euros: every decision you make moves expected margin, and you'll see it within days.

  • Build, don't advise: you'll ship agents, models and automations, not recommendations. You get frontier AI tools, our data platform and engineers who build with you.

  • Direct line to leadership: you'll present growth performance every week and shape decisions at company level.

  • A rare combination: strategy, data, marketing and AI engineering in a single seat. The steepest learning curve we can offer.

  • A path that grows with the system: from operator to architect to leader of growth automation at Zefir.

 

Who you are

  • Top-tier problem solver: 2 to 6 years at a top strategy consultancy (BCG, McKinsey, Bain...), in Growth, Ops or Strategy at a high-growth tech company, or both. You structure messy problems in minutes and you get the math right the first time.

  • Builder at heart: you have already built something real: a model, a tool, an automation, an AI agent, a side project. SQL is second nature; Python is a strong plus. You'd rather prototype in an afternoon than debate for a week.

  • Commercial instinct: you think in revenue, not in vanity metrics. You're curious about why people click, book and buy, and you know when fewer leads is good news.

  • Systems thinker: when you see a task done twice, you design the system that removes it. You care about guardrails, feedback loops and what happens when things break.

  • Ownership and clarity: you hold a high bar, move fast and own outcomes. You write crisp updates that start with the number, the cause and the action.

  • Languages: fluency in French and English is required.

  • What we don't require: years of media buying or a marketing title. We hire for slope, not intercept: if you learn fast and build relentlessly, we'll teach you the rest.

 

Hiring process

  • 30-min call with our Talent Lead

  • 30-min interview with the hiring manager

  • 60-min live case on real (anonymised) funnel data. AI is allowed in part of the case: we want to see how you use it.

  • 15-min coffee chat with our RevOps lead and 45-min Behavioral interview with our CoFounder, then references


Benefits

The following is for permanent employees only. For other contracts (interns, apprentices, fixed-term..), please, check with your recruiter.

  • Competitive salary: You can run your own simulation with our salary calculator.

  • BSPCE (Stock Options): Available for everyone, with monthly vesting after year one, over a 4-year period.

  • Healthcare plan: Full coverage with Alan for team members, their partners, and children.

  • Office in Le Peletier, Paris (9th arrondissement): With flexible remote work options.

  • Swile meal card: €11 per worked day.

  • Swile mobility card: €45/month to support sustainable transportation (metro, carpooling, biking…).

  • Team events: Monthly Mixers to connect and share good times, and quarterly All Hands to celebrate wins across the company.

Our Operating Principles

🏔️ Steep Mountains Are Steep: Setting ambitious goals and working hard to achieve them.

🌊 Ride Reality: Actively seeking challenges and thriving by adapting flexibly to changes.

🏀 Play for the Front of the Jersey: Prioritizing team success over individual recognition.

Application & Process

rawCandidates.title: AI Deployment Manager, Enterprise
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
We believe conversations will become the #1 way to shop.

At Gorgias, we’re building the platform that makes this real: a unified AI agent that sells, supports, and re-engages customers across the entire journey. Conversational Commerce is the future of ecommerce, and we’re leading that shift.

Our mission is to turn every interaction between a brand and its customers into a relationship: personal, seamless, and intelligent. By combining deep product expertise with the latest in AI, we’re making shopping feel more natural, human, and connected than ever before.

To win, we focus relentlessly on:

  • Quality: conversations that feel authentic and on-brand.

  • Experience: effortless shopping from chat to checkout.

  • Re-engagement: personal, 1-1 dialogue instead of noisy marketing.

The opportunity is massive. As AI reshapes how people buy, Gorgias is building the foundation for the next decade of ecommerce, where every brand has its own intelligent agent and every customer feels understood.

Join us to make Conversational Commerce real.

About the Team

The AI Deployment (Customer Implementation) Team at Gorgias is dedicated to ensuring a seamless and successful start for every customer's journey with our products. Our primary objective is to elevate the onboarding experience by delivering a white-glove service and expert guidance to our customers. This involves cultivating a heightened proficiency in product knowledge, engaging in consultative conversations, and adopting a strategic implementation approach that extends beyond mere activation. Our mission is to empower companies to launch swiftly and effectively on Gorgias, showcasing the exceptional value of our flagship products: Helpdesk and AI Agent.

Our team plays a pivotal role in the overall success of our products, influencing customer adoption, usage, and retention. As AI becomes central to how merchants support their customers, we're at the forefront of helping businesses unlock automation, configure AI Agent, and drive measurable outcomes from day one. By fostering meaningful connections with our customers, we contribute to the sustained growth and satisfaction of businesses leveraging Gorgias solutions.

 

About the Role

As the AI Deployment Manager, your role is to manage the entire onboarding process for your book of business, beginning to end - from sales handover through configuration, training, and activation. As the first point of contact, this role is instrumental in managing all aspects of customer relations post-sales stage.

You will actively contribute to our mission of providing a white-glove onboarding experience, showcasing the value of our flagship products, Helpdesk and AI Agent. The perfect fit for this role is an adept professional with a consultative mindset and a strategic approach to onboarding.

 

What You'll Do

  • Conduct in-depth discovery and implementation sessions for your book of business, tailoring the experience to drive adoption and usage of our Helpdesk and AI Agent products.

  • Build on behalf of the customer, utilizing a consultative approach to customize solutions that align with their specific needs and goals.

  • Design and drive AI Agent adoption roadmaps for each customer, sequencing automation rollout to support change management and prove value at each stage.

  • Drive the activation ratio and reduce time to value through a white-glove experience, providing expert guidance on both Helpdesk and AI Agent configuration.

  • Establish trust with customers by demonstrating expert knowledge of our products, sharing best practices, and communicating the business impact of AI adoption in clear, compelling terms.

  • Act as the primary liaison between customers and internal teams, ensuring seamless communication and cross-functional accountability throughout the onboarding process.

  • Manage integrations with the customer's ecommerce tech stack; explore feasibility of custom integration paths and troubleshoot proactively using available technical resources and AI tools.

  • Drive project timelines through clear milestone setting and workback schedules, ensuring effective project management throughout the implementation.

  • Analyze and interpret e-commerce customer data to build compelling, executive-ready narratives - translating support metrics and AI Agent outcomes into business impact framed around revenue, efficiency, and risk, so that CEOs and CFOs become champions, not blockers.

  • Document customer interactions, configurations, and learnings meticulously - contributing insights that improve future implementations and team best practices.

  • Proactively identify and mitigate roadblocks to decrease time to value, and coach L1/L2 peers by sharing patterns, playbooks, and implementation learnings.

  • Leverage AI tools to accelerate discovery synthesis, solution design, and documentation.

 

Who You Are

  • Experience: 3–5+ years in SaaS as an implementation manager or similar post-sales role, driving adoption and activation with a demonstrated track record of independently delivering complex implementations. Ecommerce experience is a strong plus.

  • Consultancy and Project Management: 3–5+ years crafting and overseeing project timelines tailored to enhance activation among merchants, encompassing strategic recommendations and actionable suggestions. Comfortable managing 25-30 accounts simultaneously with a high degree of autonomy.

  • Communication Skills: Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and executive presence. You build compelling narratives that resonate at the CEO and CFO level - translating complex data and AI outcomes into clear business impact, overcoming objections before they become roadblocks, and turning skeptics into champions. You adapt your message and materials to any audience.

  • Technical Curiosity: You understand how ecommerce platforms and integrations work, you're comfortable exploring how to build or troubleshoot integrations, and you default to resourcefulness over escalation. Familiarity with Shopify and common ecommerce tech stacks is a strong plus.

  • AI & Automation Mindset: Passionate about technology, automation, and the future of AI in customer support. Comfortable configuring AI Agent, discussing automation strategy with merchants, and learning new AI capabilities quickly. Proactively uses tools like Claude to improve your own efficiency.

  • Adaptability and Learning Agility: Thrives in an evolving onboarding process, demonstrating adaptability to change, quick learning, and the ability to keep up with new product developments and process changes.

  • Relationship Building: Passionate about building and maintaining relationships, with a focus on driving engagement, product adoption, and mitigating churn.

  • Passion for Learning: Demonstrated passion for continuous learning and personal growth. You stay current on Gorgias product developments and ecommerce trends, and you actively contribute to team knowledge.

  • French Bilingual (C1) is a must

AI at Gorgias
At Gorgias, AI is a natural extension of how we work and build. Our teams use it every day to research, write, analyze, code, and craft better customer experiences. Everyone has access to premium AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Granola & others) and an annual L&D budget to explore new ones.

The real magic happens when we share what we learn. Our #powerup Slack channel is a digital petri dish of new tools and workflows, and each team has AI champions who showcase fresh ideas during weekly company-wide standups, now practically AI demo sessions.

We see AI not as a replacement for creativity or empathy, but as a multiplier, helping us move faster, think deeper, and serve customers better.

AI use in Recruiting at Gorgias

Diversity & Inclusion at Gorgias
